question_text: A team hosts hundreds of small, infrequently-invoked fine-tuned models on SageMaker AI and wants to avoid paying for a dedicated endpoint per model while still serving any of them on demand. Which SageMaker deployment option best fits?

options.text: SageMaker multi-model endpoint — many models share one endpoint and are loaded on demand
One single-model real-time endpoint per model
Bedrock on-demand InvokeModel
A separate Lambda function packaging each model

explanation: A SageMaker multi-model endpoint hosts many models behind one endpoint, dynamically loading a model into memory when invoked — cost-efficient for large numbers of small, infrequently-used models. One endpoint per model multiplies cost; Bedrock serves managed FMs, not your many custom fine-tuned models; packaging large models in Lambda hits size/latency limits.
source_topic: SageMaker multi-model endpoints for many small models

question_text: Several models must share the same SageMaker endpoint's GPU fleet, but each model needs its OWN independent auto-scaling policy and resource allocation. Which SageMaker capability provides per-model scaling on a shared endpoint?

options.text: SageMaker Inference Components — each model gets its own scaling policy and resource share on a shared endpoint
A multi-model endpoint with a single shared scaling policy
Bedrock Provisioned Throughput
Amazon EC2 Spot Instances

explanation: SageMaker Inference Components let you deploy multiple models to one endpoint where each component has its own scaling policy and allocated compute, maximizing GPU utilization with independent scaling. A plain multi-model endpoint shares one scaling policy; Bedrock Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity for managed FMs; Spot Instances are a pricing model, not a per-model scaling mechanism.

question_text: When deploying a large language model on SageMaker AI for high-throughput inference, which model server was created by Amazon specifically for serving deep learning models (and is commonly highlighted for this platform)?

options.text: DJL Serving (Deep Java Library)
Apache Kafka
nginx
Redis

explanation: DJL Serving (Deep Java Library) is an Amazon-created model server used with SageMaker AI for high-performance deep-learning inference; other supported servers include TorchServe and Triton Inference Server. Kafka is a streaming platform, nginx is a web server/proxy, and Redis is an in-memory data store — none are DL model servers.

question_text: Before promoting a new model version to production, a team wants to send it a copy of real live production traffic to compare its behaviour against the current model — WITHOUT returning the new model's responses to users. Which SageMaker capability does this?

options.text: SageMaker shadow testing — mirror live traffic to the new (shadow) variant while only the production variant serves users
A/B testing that splits real user responses 50/50
Blue/green deployment with an immediate full cutover
Batch transform on a static dataset

explanation: Shadow testing mirrors a copy of production traffic to a shadow variant and records its behaviour for comparison, while users continue to receive only the production model's responses — a zero-user-impact validation. A/B testing actually serves the new variant to some users; blue/green cutover switches live traffic; batch transform uses a static dataset, not mirrored live traffic.
source_topic: SageMaker shadow testing with mirrored traffic

question_text: A self-hosted model on SageMaker AI real-time endpoints experiences highly variable traffic, and the team wants the endpoint to add and remove instance capacity automatically based on load. Which mechanism provides this?

options.text: Auto scaling policies on the SageMaker endpoint (target-tracking on invocation metrics)
Manually resizing the endpoint each morning
Bedrock cross-region inference
Increasing the model's temperature parameter

explanation: SageMaker AI endpoints support auto scaling with target-tracking policies (e.g. on invocations-per-instance), adding/removing instances automatically as load varies. Manual resizing is not automatic and misses spikes; Bedrock cross-region inference applies to managed Bedrock FMs, not your SageMaker endpoint capacity; temperature is an inference parameter unrelated to scaling.
